previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted after a mechanical fall resulting in a right intertrochanteric hip fracture, which was repaired with cephalomedullary nailing. Postoperatively, she developed hypotension and troponin elevation consistent with a Type 2 NSTEMI, managed with aspirin, heparin, and beta-blocker up-titration. A pharmacologic stress test revealed new reversible ischemia in the RCA and LAD territories, but cardiology recommended medical management over intervention. She experienced postoperative ileus with colonic distention, managed conservatively with bowel regimen adjustment. Her chronic ITP led to transient postoperative thrombocytopenia without significant bleeding, and she received a single-unit blood transfusion for anemia in the setting of CAD. An asymptomatic UTI was treated with a short course of ciprofloxacin. Renal function, initially impaired, normalized with diuresis. She was discharged to rehabilitation with optimized cardiac and pain medications, DVT prophylaxis with heparin, and close follow-up plans.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is an ___ y/o female with a past medical history of 
CAD s/p PCI DES to ___ and DES to distal-LAD ___, type A 
aortic dissection s/p repair ___, chronic ___, h/o breast 
cancer, and ITP who presents with chest pain.  

# NSTEMI: The patient presented with chest pain radiating to 
arm/jaw worsened with activity and relieved with NG, concerning 
for ACS. Troponin elevated to 0.30 on admission (peaked at 
0.46). EKG showed T-wave inversions in V4-V6 similar to prior 
and T-wave normalization in V1-V3 c/f NSTEMI. Patient also noted 
to have pain worsened with inspiration in the setting of 
elevated d-dimer and therefore PE was  on the differential. Exam 
negative for calf tenderness or unilateral calf swelling and the 
patient was breathing comfortably on room air. TTE showed LVEF 
60% with nml biventricular cavity sizes and preserved global 
biventricular systolic function without evidence of RV strain. 
Given her clinical presentation, known cardiac disease and 
elevated troponin, the patient was managed for an NSTEMI. While 
the patient has a documented heparin allergy, review of her 
record revealed a low PF4 OD and negative SRA making HITT 
unlikely. She was started on heparin gtt without complications. 
The patient was taken to cath on ___ which demonstrated 
chronically occluded RCA, 95% LAD stenosis which was ballooned, 
and tortuous left Cx. The decision was made to not stent the LAD 
lesion given underlying ITP and current platelet count of 
80,000. She tolerated the procedure well without any reaction to 
the contrast load (please see below for the pre-treatment 
regimen) and the patient was discharged on Plavix 75mg daily x1 
month duration and ASA 81mg to be continued indefinitely. Her 
home dose of imdur was increased to 60mg daily and she was 
continued on atorvastatin 80mg daily, metoprolol 100mg PO, 
amlodipine 2.5mg daily, spironolactone 12.5mg daily, and 
torsemide 60mg daily.

# Chronic dCHF: LVEF=60% on TTE. The patient appeared euvolemic 
on examination without evidence of pulmonary edema on CXR. Her 
daily weights and I/Os were monitored and the patient was 
continued on her home torsemide 60mg daily, spironolactone 
12.5mg daily, metoprolol, ASA and statin. Her dose of imdur was 
increased to 60mg daily.  

# Leukocytosis: The patient WBC increased from 11 to 25 after 
receiving large dose of steroids for pre-treatment for contrast 
allergy prior to cath. Afebrile and no signs or symptoms of 
infection.    
   
# ITP: Platelet count within baseline level of 70-100 throughout 
her hospitalization. No signs of active bleed and HD stable. Her 
platelet counts were closely monitored and the decision was made 
to not place a DES to prevent prolonged anti-platelet therapy 
with Plavix. The patient was discharged home on a short 1 month 
course of Plavix s/p angioplasty to the LAD.

# HTN: Continued on home amlodipine, metop, aldactone and 
torsemide. Increased imdur to 60mg daily. 

# Contrast Allergy: The patient had an anaphylactic reaction to 
contrast in ___. Per allergy, the patient was placed on the 
following regimen and tolerated the cath without complications:
 - Prednisone 40mg 13h, 7h, and 1h prior to procedure
 - Zyrtec 10mg night prior to and in the AM of procedure
 - Benadryl 25mg in the AM prior to procedure    

# Recurrent falls: Patient reports feeling unsteady on her feet 
with h/o falls. Neuro exam benign and CT head negative for 
bleed. The patient was seen by physical therapy and was able to 
ambulate without difficulty. Cleared for home upon discharge.
